patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a small boxed two-line icon in the top-right of the header, a conventional collapsed navigation trigger on narrow screens.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close the primary navigation panel or menu links for mobile. The trigger should reflect expanded/collapsed state and likely reveal the hidden site sections shown more openly on desktop.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a dropdown, slide-in drawer, or full-screen overlay.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows multiple short nav labels across the top and additional grouped link text beneath the header area, implying expandable navigation categories or secondary menus.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Top-level nav items should reveal submenu links on click or hover, matching the extra link rows suggested below the main nav. Active/open state should be visually indicated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear which top-level items have submenus, whether interaction is hover or click first, and whether only one menu stays open at a time.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a large bordered content block separated from the surrounding page; in the mobile sketch it resembles a distinct overlay/card with isolated content and CTA, and the reference HTML strongly suggests image lightbox/cart overlay behavior on this product page.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A triggered overlay is likely needed for at least one major action such as viewing the product image larger or opening cart/details. It should open above page content, trap focus, and close via explicit dismiss action and Escape.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw a close icon or dimmed backdrop, so this could also be an inline panel rather than a true modal.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The product area includes a prominent CTA/button and form-like structure in the lower content block, consistent with quantity/add-to-cart or contact/purchase input behavior on a product page.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Any quantity or purchase-related input should validate before submission, prevent invalid values, and surface inline errors or status if submission fails. If there is a required field, focus should move to the invalid control.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not clearly expose the exact fields, so validation scope is inferred from the product-page layout and CTA.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop header includes compact utility text at top right and a bottom-wide bar with small text at both ends, consistent with a cart/status area that can update after actions.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Cart item count, subtotal, or status text should update dynamically after add/remove actions without full page reload. Updates should be announced accessibly if they change in response to user actions.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly label the changing text as cart count versus another status indicator.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The product-focused layout with a strong CTA implies immediate feedback after actions like Add to Cart; the isolated lower card area suggests transient confirmation messaging may appear near the action.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: After successful add-to-cart or similar action, a brief confirmation message should appear and dismiss automatically or be manually dismissible.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit toast is drawn; this is inferred from expected ecommerce interaction rather than a clearly sketched component.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile hamburger and the likely overlay/modal interactions imply components that open and close, requiring managed keyboard focus. Desktop dropdowns also imply controlled focus movement.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When menus or overlays open, focus should move into them appropriately; when they close, focus should return to the triggering control. Keyboard navigation through open menus should be logical and visible.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Exact focus targets depend on whether the hidden content is a drawer, dropdown, or modal.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a relatively light but important layer of JavaScript centered on ecommerce/product interactions rather than complex app-like widgets. Mobile primarily depends on a collapsed navigation trigger and careful focus handling for hidden content, while desktop more strongly suggests exposed top navigation with expandable secondary links and a dynamically updating utility/cart area. A product action flow is implied in both views, so validation and user feedback behaviors are likely necessary even where fields are only loosely sketched.
